key_features.classic_presentation: Ectopic pregnancy presents with UNILATERAL LOWER ABDOMINAL/PELVIC PAIN in a woman of CHILDBEARING AGE with MISSED PERIOD or abnormal vaginal bleeding. Pain is initially crampy, becoming sharp if rupture occurs. Onset is 6-8 weeks after last menstrual period. MUST BE RULED OUT in ANY female of childbearing age with abdominal pain. Key associated symptoms: Vaginal spotting or bleeding (lighter than normal period), dizziness, shoulder pain (if ruptured with hemoperitoneum irritating diaphragm). Location: Unilateral adnexal pain, sometimes cervical motion tenderness. Key history: Prior ectopic, PID history, IUD use, tubal surgery. PREGNANCY TEST POSITIVE. If RUPTURED: sudden severe pain, lightheadedness, syncope, peritoneal signs. Key positives: Positive pregnancy test, unilateral pain, vaginal bleeding. Key negatives: Negative pregnancy test essentially rules out ectopic.

red_flags: LIFE-THREATENING if ruptured - sudden severe pain with hypotension/syncope - call 911
Shoulder pain with abdominal pain in pregnant woman - ruptured ectopic with hemoperitoneum
Positive pregnancy test + abdominal pain - ALWAYS get ultrasound to rule out ectopic
ANY female of childbearing age with abdominal pain needs pregnancy test
